newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Madikizela-Mandela backs call over spies.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Madikizela-Mandela backs call over spies.

text.p: South Africa's Winnie Madikizela-Mandela on Friday backed a call by her former husband, President Nelson Mandela, for African National Congress members who served as informers for the apartheid government to be exposed.
Allegations surfaced recently during inquiries by Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu's "truth commission" that up to five ANC cabinet ministers had spied on their own colleagues.

"Let us stop those covert counter-revolutionary third forces in their tracks through, amongst others, full public disclosure! Expose the spies!," Madikizela-Mandela said in an emotive speech to up to 1,000 supporters in Sharpeville.
The rally was held in the a black township, where 69 black demonstrators were killed by police in 1960, to mark Human Rights Day, a public holiday in South Africa.
Mandela said earlier this month that his government did not wish to protect individuals proven to have served the apartheid regime, even if they belonged to his ruling party.
Mandela has also said that anyone whose actions led to deaths would be fired.

The Truth and Reconciliation Commission's amnesty committee initially ruled that spies identified during applications for immunity from prosecution for human rights crimes would not be publicly named.
But Tutu later said it would be necessary to name the people implicated after giving them 21 days' notice in order to halt the spread of lies and innuendo.
The outcome will be a test for Mandela's ANC, which has promoted open government and transparency in politics since it won power in the country's first all-race elections in 1994.
